questions.q: Information is
o: data that has been processed and given meaning
questions.why: Data + context = information.

questions.q: Batch processing suits
questions.why: Real-time processing suits bookings and control.

questions.q: Which is an example of information rather than data?
o: The average temperature this week was 31 °C
A list of numbers with no labels
questions.why: Information is data given context and meaning.

long.q: Compare batch processing and real-time processing, giving a suitable use for each.
scheme: B1: batch: data collected and processed together later, without user interaction
B1: use: payroll / utility bills
B1: real-time: data processed immediately as it arrives
B1: use: booking systems / control systems

questions.q: A compiler
o: translates the whole program before it runs
translates line by line as it runs
questions.why: An interpreter works line by line.

questions.q: A device driver is:
o: Software that lets the operating system communicate with a hardware device
questions.why: Examiners (2023): the most common mistake was to consider a device driver to be hardware.

questions.q: Which software controls the hardware and provides a user interface?
questions.why: Device drivers let the operating system talk to particular hardware.

long.q: Compare a compiler and an interpreter.
scheme: B1: a compiler translates the whole source code into machine code before it runs
B1: it produces an executable that runs without the translator, and runs faster
B1: an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time
B1: it stops at the first error, which helps debugging, but the program runs more slowly and needs the interpreter every time

questions.q: In a control system, an actuator
o: carries out a physical action, e.g. opens a window
questions.why: Sensors measure; actuators act.

questions.q: In a computer-controlled greenhouse, what does the microprocessor do with a sensor reading?
o: Compares it with a preset value and switches an actuator if needed
questions.why: Monitoring only records; control acts on the readings in a feedback loop.

questions.q: Why is an ADC needed in many monitoring systems?
o: Sensors give analogue signals that the computer must receive in digital form
questions.why: A DAC is used when the computer drives an analogue device.

long.q: A greenhouse uses a computer to control temperature. Describe how the system works.
scheme: B1: a temperature sensor measures temperature continuously
B1: an ADC converts the analogue reading to digital
B1: the microprocessor compares the reading with a preset value
B1: if too high, it sends a signal to an actuator to open a window / start a fan
B1: the process repeats continuously (feedback)

questions.q: In a flowchart, a decision is shown by
questions.why: Rectangles are processes; parallelograms are input/output.

questions.q: In a flowchart, a decision box must have:
o: A Yes and a No output
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates are reminded every decision box needs Yes and No outputs, using mathematical expressions rather than text.

questions.q: Which flowchart symbol shows a decision?
o: A diamond with Yes and No exits
questions.why: Examiners (2023): every decision box needs a Yes and a No output.

long.q: Draw a flowchart that inputs the marks of 20 students one at a time and, for each, outputs 'Pass' if the mark is 50 or more, otherwise 'Fail'.
scheme: B1: start and stop terminators
B1: a counter set to 0 and incremented each time
B1: input of the mark in a parallelogram
B1: decision Mark >= 50 with Yes/No branches to the correct outputs
B1: a loop back until 20 marks have been processed

questions.q: Which is a safety risk rather than a health risk?
questions.why: Safety risks cause accidents.

questions.q: Which is a way to reduce the risk of repetitive strain injury?
o: Use a wrist rest and take regular breaks
questions.why: Health risks need health measures, not security measures.

questions.q: What is phishing?
o: Hacking a Wi-Fi password by guessing
Fake messages that try to trick people into giving personal details
questions.why: Check the sender and never follow links asking for passwords.

long.q: Explain the difference between a health risk and a safety risk when using IT, giving one example of each and a precaution for each.
scheme: B1: a health risk harms the body over time, e.g. RSI or eye strain
B1: a precaution, e.g. regular breaks; ergonomic keyboard; anti-glare screen
B1: a safety risk can cause injury at once, e.g. electrocution, fire from overloaded sockets, tripping over cables
B1: a precaution, e.g. cable ducts; not overloading sockets; a CO₂ extinguisher nearby

questions.q: The digital divide is
o: the gap between those with and without access to technology
questions.why: Caused by income, location, age, education.

questions.q: What is the digital divide?
o: The split between hardware and software
The gap between people who have access to IT and the internet and those who don't
questions.why: Causes include income, location, age and education.

questions.q: Which would most help to reduce the digital divide in a rural area?
o: Providing affordable broadband and community IT access
questions.why: Access and skills both matter.

long.q: Explain two causes of the digital divide within a country, and one way a government could reduce it.
scheme: B1: a cause, e.g. income: poorer households can't afford devices or broadband
B1: a second cause, e.g. location: rural areas lack broadband infrastructure; age or education: lack of digital skills
B1: a measure, e.g. funding rural broadband; subsidised devices; free digital-skills courses
B1: explained: how it gives the excluded group access or skills

questions.q: What does a VPN do?
o: creates an encrypted connection over a public network
questions.why: Virtual private network.

questions.q: What does a router do?
o: Connects devices in a LAN by broadcasting to all
Forwards data packets between different networks using IP addresses
questions.why: Examiners (2023): there was confusion between switches, routers and hubs.

questions.q: What does a switch do in a LAN?
o: Sends data only to the device it is addressed to, using MAC addresses
Connects the LAN to the internet
questions.why: A hub sends to every device.

long.q: A small business wants staff working from home to use the office network securely. Explain how a VPN would help.
scheme: B1: it creates an encrypted tunnel across the internet
B1: so data that is intercepted can't be read
B1: staff appear to be on the office network, so they can use shared files and services

questions.q: The inference engine of an expert system
o: applies rules to the knowledge base to reach conclusions
questions.why: The reasoning part.

questions.q: Which part of an expert system applies rules to the facts to reach a conclusion?
questions.why: The knowledge base holds the facts and the rule base the IF…THEN rules.

questions.q: Which is a use of an expert system?
questions.why: Others: mineral prospecting, car fault diagnosis, financial planning.

long.q: Describe the components of an expert system used for medical diagnosis and how it reaches a conclusion.
scheme: B1: knowledge base: facts about illnesses and symptoms
B1: rules base: IF–THEN rules
B1: inference engine applies the rules to the facts and the user's answers
B1: user interface asks questions (e.g. symptoms) and shows the diagnosis
B1: explanation system shows how the conclusion was reached, often with a probability

questions.q: VLOOKUP searches
o: the first column of a table for a value and returns one from another column
questions.why: Vertical lookup.

questions.q: A spreadsheet formula should refer to:
o: A cell reference holding the value
questions.why: Examiners (2023): the formula had to reference a cell rather than a value.

questions.q: A formula is copied down a column but must keep using cell B1. Which reference is used?
questions.why: Absolute references don't change when copied.

long.q: A sheet named Prices holds product codes in A2:A50 and prices in C2:C50. On another sheet, B2 holds a product code. Write a formula for C2 that returns the matching price and can be copied down, and explain each part.
scheme: B1: =VLOOKUP(B2,Prices!$A$2:$C$50,3,FALSE)
B1: B2 is the value looked up (the product code)
B1: the absolute range stays fixed when copied; column 3 returns the price
B1: FALSE returns an exact match only

questions.q: A foreign key
o: links a record to the primary key of another table
is unique in its own table
questions.why: Used to create relationships.

questions.q: Normalisation aims to
questions.why: Removes repeated data and anomalies.

questions.q: In normalisation to third normal form, a table must have:
o: No non-key field that depends on another non-key field
questions.why: Examiners (2023): descriptions of normalisation often lacked detail.

long.q: The table Bookings(BookingID, CustomerID, CustomerName, CustomerPhone, RoomNo, BookingDate) is not in third normal form. Explain why, and normalise it.
scheme: B1: CustomerName and CustomerPhone depend on CustomerID, not on the key BookingID (a non-key dependency)
B1: Customers(CustomerID, CustomerName, CustomerPhone) with CustomerID as primary key
B1: Bookings(BookingID, CustomerID, RoomNo, BookingDate) with BookingID as primary key
B1: CustomerID in Bookings is a foreign key linking to Customers

questions.q: Lossy compression
o: permanently removes some data to reduce file size
questions.why: e.g. MP3, MP4.

questions.q: Why is a sound file normalised (amplified to just below the maximum)?
o: To make it as loud as possible without clipping
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many amplified past the maximum, clipping the waveform.

questions.q: What is a transition in video editing?
o: An effect used to move from one clip to the next
questions.why: Examples: fade, wipe, dissolve.

long.q: Explain the difference between lossy and lossless compression of an audio file, and say which you would use for a podcast streamed to mobile phones, with a reason.
scheme: B1: lossy permanently removes data (sounds people hear least), e.g. MP3
B1: lossless shrinks the file without losing data, so the original can be rebuilt exactly, e.g. FLAC
B1: lossy for the podcast
B1: smaller files stream faster and use less mobile data; for speech the loss is barely noticeable

questions.q: Augmented reality
o: overlays digital content on the real world
questions.why: VR replaces; AR overlays.

questions.q: Which is an emerging technology?
questions.why: Others include 3D printing, virtual reality and AI.

questions.q: What is augmented reality?
o: Computer images laid over a live view of the real world
questions.why: Virtual reality replaces the real view completely.

long.q: Discuss the use of augmented reality (AR) in education.
scheme: B1: AR overlays computer-generated images on the real world, seen through a phone, tablet or headset
B1: benefit: makes abstract ideas visible, e.g. 3D models of organs or molecules
B1: benefit: interactive and engaging; safe practice of tasks
B1: drawback: cost of devices and content; not every student has a suitable device
B1: drawback: can distract; eye strain or motion sickness
B1: a reasoned conclusion

topics.name: Role and impact of IT in society

questions.q: Which is an impact of online banking on society?
o: fewer bank branches and less face-to-face service
questions.why: Convenience with social costs.

questions.q: Which is a negative impact of IT on employment?
o: Some jobs are replaced by automation
questions.why: Discuss both sides when asked about impact.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of online banking for customers?
o: Banking at any time without travelling
questions.why: Answer from the viewpoint the question asks for.

long.q: Evaluate the impact of online shopping on customers and on high-street shops.
scheme: B1: customers: wider choice and easy price comparison
B1: customers: shop at any time with home delivery, helpful for people with limited mobility
B1: customers: risk of fraud, can't inspect goods, returns are less convenient
B1: shops: fewer visitors, leading to closures and job losses
B1: shops that adapt, e.g. click-and-collect or their own websites
B1: a reasoned judgement

questions.q: TCP/IP is
o: the set of protocols the internet uses
questions.why: Transmission Control Protocol / Internet Protocol.

questions.q: What is a WAN?
o: A network covering a large geographical area
questions.why: The internet is the largest WAN.

questions.q: Which transmission medium is least affected by electrical interference?
questions.why: It carries light rather than electrical signals.

long.q: Two office buildings 2 km apart are to be connected. Compare fibre-optic cable with copper cable for this link.
scheme: B1: fibre has much higher bandwidth
B1: fibre carries signals much further with less attenuation, so fewer repeaters
B1: fibre is unaffected by electromagnetic interference and is harder to tap
B1: copper is cheaper and easier to install but suits shorter runs, so fibre suits 2 km

questions.q: A Gantt chart shows
questions.why: Used to schedule and track a project.

questions.q: The critical path is
o: the longest sequence of dependent tasks
questions.why: It sets the shortest possible project duration.

questions.q: In project management, a deliverable is:
o: A resource delivered for a task
A measurable output produced at the end of a stage
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many described deliverables as resources that had to be delivered.

long.q: Explain how a Gantt chart helps a project manager.
scheme: B1: shows each task against a timeline
B1: shows dependencies and the critical path
B1: helps allocate resources and spot clashes
B1: progress can be tracked against the plan

questions.q: Black-box testing checks
o: inputs and outputs without looking at the code
questions.why: White-box testing looks at internal logic.

questions.q: In the system life cycle, what happens during analysis?
o: The current system is studied and requirements are identified
questions.why: Methods include interviews, questionnaires and observation.

questions.q: Which changeover method runs the old and new systems together?
questions.why: It is safe but costly in time and staff.

long.q: Describe three methods of investigating the current system during analysis, giving an advantage of each.
scheme: B1: questionnaires
B1: reach many users quickly; anonymous answers may be more honest
B1: interviews
B1: follow-up questions give detailed answers
B1: observation (or examining documents)
B1: shows what really happens rather than what people say happens

questions.q: Vector graphics
questions.why: Stored as shapes and paths.

questions.q: Why are vector graphics better than bitmaps for a logo?
o: They can be resized without losing quality
questions.why: Vectors are stored as shapes and coordinates.

questions.q: What does increasing an image's resolution do?
o: Increases the number of pixels and the file size
questions.why: Higher resolution means more detail.

long.q: Explain why a company logo should be created as a vector graphic rather than a bitmap.
scheme: B1: a vector stores shapes as mathematical objects (lines, curves, fills), not pixels
B1: it scales to any size without pixelation, from business card to billboard
B1: the file is usually smaller, and each shape is easy to edit

questions.q: In animation, tweening
questions.why: In-betweening.

questions.q: What is tweening in animation?
o: Generating the frames between two key frames
questions.why: It saves time and makes motion smooth.

questions.q: Frame rate is measured in:
questions.why: A higher frame rate gives smoother motion.

long.q: Explain what tweening is and how it saves time compared with frame-by-frame animation. An animation lasts 4 seconds at 24 frames per second: how many frames does it have?
scheme: B1: the animator sets key frames (e.g. start and end positions)
B1: the software generates the in-between frames
B1: so far fewer frames are drawn by hand, and motion is smooth
B1: 4 × 24 = 96 frames

questions.q: JavaScript in a web page is mainly used to
questions.why: HTML structure, CSS style, JavaScript behaviour.

questions.q: Which language adds interactivity to a web page in the browser?
questions.why: HTML is structure; CSS is presentation.

questions.q: In JavaScript, setInterval(f, 1000) runs f:
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates left a timer at the default 1000 ms instead of the value required.

long.q: Write JavaScript so that clicking the button with id 'go' changes the text of the paragraph with id 'msg' to 'Hello'.
scheme: B1: select the button: document.getElementById("go")
B1: attach a click handler: addEventListener("click", …) or onclick
B1: select the paragraph: document.getElementById("msg")
B1: set its innerHTML (or textContent) to "Hello"

questions.q: A mail merge field
o: is replaced with data from the source for each record
is a fixed piece of text
questions.why: e.g. «FirstName».

questions.q: What is a mail merge?
o: Combining a standard document with a data source to make personalised copies
Sending one email to one person
questions.why: Merge fields are replaced by data from each record.

questions.q: How can a mail merge send letters only to customers in one city?
o: Filter the data source on the City field
questions.why: Filters select records without changing the data.

long.q: A company wants to send a letter only to customers in Paris who have spent over €500. Describe how to set this up as a mail merge.
scheme: B1: link the master letter to the customer data source
B1: insert merge fields (e.g. name, address) in the letter
B1: filter the records: City = 'Paris' AND Spent > 500
B1: preview to check, then merge only the selected records to print or email
